A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Water-Probe and Water-Bag research. All 25 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Equations, figures, tables, and relocated sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark-identification experiments across multiple LLMs, Water-Bag evaluations, and appendix experiments on global fixed-key watermarks and rank transformation.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds EXP-Edit comparisons against another detector and experiments on five closed-source model APIs in Tables 9–11.

M1.justification: Water-Probe's prompt construction, repeated sampling, rank transformation, and z-test remain unchanged, as do Water-Contrast and Water-Bag. Appendix M explains the existing inversion constraint. Multinomial EXP-Edit is an added evaluation configuration, not a modification of the proposed detector.

E1.justification: Appendix L extends evaluation from controlled local models to five deployed APIs: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo, Gemini-1.5-flash, and Gemini-1.5-pro. Their unknown watermark status introduces a distinct deployment scenario. Existing prompt tasks and C4 coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v1 has no direct comparison against another black-box watermark-identification method. v2 adds Gloaguen et al. (2024) as an evaluated comparator against Water-Probe-v2 under both argmax and multinomial EXP-Edit sampling in Tables 9–10, supplying a previously absent comparative reference.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds a separate protocol using OPT-1.3B, EXP-Edit key length 420, temperatures 0.2–1.0, and argmax versus multinomial sampling. Gloaguen's detector receives 1,000 samples of 200 tokens; Water-Probe receives 10,000 samples of five tokens. Appendix L uses API temperature 0.7. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Tables 9–10 add a focused robustness analysis asking whether replacing deterministic EXP-Edit selection with multinomial sampling changes identification effectiveness while preserving watermark F1 and text quality. Existing temperature, sample-count, rank-transformation, and proxy-model analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The new comparison adds p-values from Gloaguen's EXP-Edit detector, identified in Appendix I as a Mann-Whitney U test. Water-Probe's three-repeat standard-deviation estimation, z-test, and confidence thresholds remain unchanged. No increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are unchanged, but Tables 9–11 add substantive comparative and deployment findings. Both detectors report p < 0.001 under argmax sampling. Under multinomial sampling, Water-Probe retains p < 0.001 throughout, while Gloaguen's p-values are 0.33 at temperature 0.3, 0.83 at 0.4, and 1.0 at 0.5–1.0. All five API tests report no detected watermark.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces v1's exact cancellation and Sim(0,0) argument with independent empirical rank estimates, Gaussian sampling-error assumptions, and an expected-zero similarity derivation in Equations 20–25. Theorem 1 and Appendix A otherwise retain their mathematics. Appendix M expands the algebra of the existing inversion constraint.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the central novelty claim from the first study of watermarked-LLM imperceptibility to the first unified identification method covering watermarking during generation. This changes the claimed contribution relative to acknowledged prior identification work. The Water-Bag contribution and broad effectiveness claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix I interprets the new sampling comparison as evidence of broader applicability than Gloaguen's detector. Appendix K explicitly bounds applicability through trustworthy-API and untampered-response assumptions. Appendix L acknowledges that unknown ground truth prevents confirming the accuracy of API classifications. Existing robustness tradeoffs and fixed-key limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an official repository link, prompt-design guidance in Appendix J, inversion-calculation details in Appendix M, and query budgets and API-date information for the new experiments. Existing concrete prompts and MarkLLM documentation remain. The PDFs establish added access information, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 introduces Gloaguen et al. (2024) as the closest prior work and substantially develops the comparison in the introduction, Section 6, and Appendix I. Positioning shifts toward unified identification and broader sampling applicability. Several peripheral citations and discussions, including UPV, WaterSeeker, and translation robustness, are removed.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, the introduction's contribution bullets are removed, several introductory passages are shortened, and prompt notation is standardized. Author/header details change and new appendices receive structured explanations. Most existing prose and the methodological narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–11 and explanatory prompt boxes, compacts Table 5, relocates Tables 6–8, and colors citations and cross-references. Existing Figures 1–5 retain their visual content, with limited caption edits such as changing KTH to Exp-Edit in Figure 2. These are targeted presentation changes.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a useful comparison with the closest prior identifier in Tables 9–10 and improves practical clarity through prompt guidance, access information, and explicit deployment assumptions. These address gaps in comparative context and documentation. The gain remains limited: API tests lack ground truth, and the revised Appendix B asserts Gaussian rank errors without establishing that assumption, leaving theoretical limitations unresolved.
